taxonomy.note: The source-pool Texas concept is outdated after the 2022 Clematis reticulata-complex revision. Current C. reticulata s.s. is not a Texas native in Kew's backbone. Historical East Texas records may resolve to C. arenicola, but no Hays/target-zone occurrence is inferred.

evidence: Current Kew/POWO re-circumscribes Clematis reticulata sensu stricto to the southeastern U.S. and lists Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, and South Carolina — not Texas.

Murphy, Harris & Estes (2022) demonstrated that the former broad Clematis reticulata complex contains six species and described Clematis arenicola for the West Gulf Coastal Plain lineage occurring into eastern Texas.

The source pool's Hays-local flag under Clematis reticulata is not counted: Hays County lies well outside the modern East-Texas/West-Gulf concept of C. arenicola and the current Kew range of C. reticulata s.s.; this record requires source-level re-identification rather than automatic synonym transfer.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Modern taxonomy/range no longer supports Clematis reticulata sensu stricto as Texas native; source-pool Hays record requires re-identification.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide range, ecoregion, cultivation, plant sales, or an unreconciled historical taxonomic concept.

morphology.look_here_first: Do not learn the old Texas 'reticulata' card as a Central Texas species. First verify geography and modern taxonomy; true C. reticulata s.s. is an southeastern Coastal Plain species east of Texas, while Texas members of the old complex require re-identification.
diagnostic_traits: historical broad concept: nodding urn-shaped leatherflower
finely and prominently reticulate leathery leaflets were a key old-field character
modern species limits require geography plus quantitative leaf venation, pubescence, pedicel and reproductive characters
true C. reticulata s.s. is re-circumscribed away from Texas
West Gulf Coastal Plain Texas material formerly called C. reticulata may belong to C. arenicola

confusers.separator: C. arenicola is the 2022-recognized West Gulf Coastal Plain lineage extending into eastern Texas; it is not automatically a synonym for every historical Texas/Hays C. reticulata record.
Pitcheri remains the locally relevant Central Texas reticulate-leaved leatherflower; use flower/sepal characters, achene beak, and geography rather than the old broad 'reticulata' label.

photo_verification.joey_media_note: No exact Clematis Joey media package was present in the canonical repo at B006 review time; Joey index lists Clematis drummondii/texensis recovery as upcoming work.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project target-zone native unless later evidence changes the decision or Calvin explicitly approves an exception.
